claims.text: HEA coating wear performance is primarily governed by intrinsic lattice distortion.
Intrinsic lattice distortion impedes dislocation mobility.
Intrinsic lattice distortion promotes formation of a stable, hard tribolayer during sliding.
The initial HEA coating has a single-phase microstructure.
The initial HEA coating exhibits significant lattice distortion arising from its multiple principal elements.
Controlled heat treatment can reduce lattice distortion without changing the alloy's overall phase or composition.
High lattice distortion in the as-deposited HEA delays the onset of plastic deformation by restricting dislocation mobility.
Restricted dislocation mobility facilitates localized formation of a mechanically robust tribolayer.
Reducing lattice distortion eases dislocation motion.
Reducing lattice distortion alters tribolayer formation and lowers wear resistance.
Heat-treated coatings with lower lattice distortion will form a less stable or thinner tribolayer than untreated coatings.
Heat-treated coatings with lower lattice distortion will have higher wear rates than untreated coatings.
Untreated HEA coatings naturally exhibit high wear resistance.
The high wear resistance of untreated HEA coatings is attributable to intrinsic lattice distortion and associated protective tribolayer development.
The proposed mechanism applies under moderate-load, room-temperature sliding conditions dominated by dislocation-mediated deformation and tribolayer formation.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under severe oxidation or other high-temperature-dominated wear regimes.
